title: Normalized descent of the strict completed scalar shift
statement: Let l be prime, E and L finite extensions of Q_l and ι:E→L a Q_l-algebra inclusion. On the small pro-etale site of any scheme Y, let C be the specified strict product-cocone scalar-extension functor, T its derived scalar extension, and e:Q_good⋙T≅C_good⋙Q the retained comparison [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension, lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined]. Every coherent integer shift structure on C descends to one on T. Flat-term K-flat representatives are stable under shifts. On every such representative P and every integer m, the descended shift, followed by e_P[m], equals T applied to the inverse Q-shift comparison, followed by e_(P[m]), the localized C-shift map and the Q-shift comparison. Thus the shifted representative is exactly the shifted cochain complex, and the zero and successive-shift laws hold globally.

proof.text: Good complexes are stable under shifts: termwise flatness is reindexed. For each acyclic test complex the signed total-tensor shift isomorphism identifies its tensor with P[m] with a shift of its tensor with P. Acyclicity is preserved by shifts and isomorphisms; hence K-flatness is preserved.

proof.text: Use site_derived_tensor_descent_independentCoefficients to localize the homotopy category of good complexes at quasi-isomorphisms. Its resolving-class equivalence with the derived category and the homotopy quotient comparison make precomposition by the good-complex localization full. Concretely, a natural transformation on good complexes is invariant under homotopy because Q factors through the homotopy quotient; descend it there and then use fully faithful whiskering by the localization.

proof.text: Precomposition is also faithful, since every derived object has a good representative. Give the good full subcategory its shifts via the fully faithful inclusion and shift stability. For a given cochain CommShift on C, form on good complexes the composite Q shift inverse, the prescribed strict comparison, the C-and-Q shift, and the inverse comparison. Full faithfulness of precomposition lifts this isomorphism to the given strict derived scalar extension.

proof.text: The zero and addition laws can be checked after precomposition. There they follow from the coherence of Q, C, and the inclusion, by cancellation of the comparison isomorphisms. Multiplying the lifted component by the prescribed comparison gives the displayed normalization. The inclusion lift comparison is the identity on the shifted complex, so the resulting shifted representative is exactly P.obj[m], with the proved good-complex property.
